items.title: Kandinsky S2V 1.0: Audio-Driven Avatar Video Generation
items.raw_content:
Authors: Nikolay Semenov, Artem Riabinin, Sergey Bassenko, Anna Averchenkova, Julia Agafonova et al.

We present Kandinsky S2V 1.0, an open family of speech-to-video models for controllable audio-driven human animation, comprising Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite (2B parameters) and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro (21B parameters). From a single reference image, a speech waveform, and a text prompt, the models generate long-form 25 FPS video in which lip motion, expression, pose, and gesture follow the speech. The architecture draws text and audio conditioning from one Qwen2.5-Omni model and adds a reference-aware three-scale visual memory. Training starts from the Kandinsky 5.0 Video foundation models [1] and combines mixed reference-memory layouts with an area-adaptive face loss. The training corpus contains 1.17M single-speaker clips selected by active-speaker detection, with captions generated directly in English and Russian. A side-by-side human evaluation against the strongest open-source baseline and two proprietary commercial models shows that Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro performs comparably to or better than these models on average and is also preferred for lip synchronization. On common speech to video benchmarks, Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro rank among the top performing models according to mean rank over five reported metrics. Beyond the base models, we provide π-Flow distilled variants of both Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro. The distilled Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro model generates video in 16 sampling steps without classifier-free guidance, achieving a 5.4 times end-to-end speedup over the base model, while matching or exceeding it on nearly all reported benchmark metrics. To accelerate open research and deployment in speech-to-video generation, we release the code, model checkpoints, and diffusers integration under the MIT license.
items.title_zh: Kandinsky S2V 1.0：音频驱动的数字人视频生成
items.summary: Kandinsky S2V 1.0 is an open speech-to-video family in 2B "Lite" and 21B "Pro" sizes that animates a single reference image from speech and a text prompt at 25 FPS, with lip motion, expression, pose and gesture following the audio. The Pro model is reported to match or surpass strong open and proprietary baselines on average and to be preferred for lip sync, and the code, checkpoints and diffusers integration are released under MIT.

items.title: Dimension-Free Scaling Laws for Size Generalization: An Exponential Separation
items.title_zh: 尺寸泛化的无维缩放定律：指数级分离
items.summary: The paper develops a statistical theory of size generalization for models on variable-size inputs such as sets and graphs, proving a sharp exponential separation in sample complexity between in-domain learning and transfer across input sizes. It derives dimension-free scaling laws, identifies an exponential source condition that restores polynomial sample complexity, and provides matching minimax lower bounds.

items.title: Predicting CVSS and CWE from CVE Descriptions with Fine-Tuned Small Language Models
items.title_zh: 用微调小语言模型从 CVE 描述预测 CVSS 与 CWE
items.summary: With NIST now enriching only high-priority CVEs, the authors fine-tune a 3.8B-parameter Phi-3.5-mini with LoRA in 2.5 hours on a single Apple M5 Pro to predict CVSS v3.1 components, severity and CWE from CVE descriptions. On 36,325 2024 CVEs, it reaches 69.9% severity accuracy and 70.9% CWE accuracy.

items.title: A Time-Synchronous Prequential Evaluation Framework for Next-Week Student Disengagement Prediction from Moodle LMS Logs
items.title_zh: 基于 Moodle LMS 日志的下一周学生投入度下降预测：时间同步序贯评估框架
items.summary: The authors build a time-synchronous prequential setup for online prediction of whether a student will disengage the following week, defined as the onset of inactivity, using Moodle logs. Across 49,329 held-out predictions, OSELM led on recall, SGD-LR on precision and specificity, and ESN on Matthews correlation coefficient and balanced accuracy.

items.title: One Bias Score, Two Factors: How Mitigations Affect Option Bias in Multiple-Choice Evaluation
items.title_zh: 一个偏差分数，两个因素：缓解措施如何影响多项选择评测中的选项偏差
items.summary: The paper links selection bias and order sensitivity in multiple-choice evaluation through a pooled standard deviation of option selection rates, which it shows factors into a flip rate and a positional skew. Across 41 checkpoints and 12 benchmarks, prior correction mainly reduces positional skew while aggregation mainly reduces flip rate, and the authors recommend reporting both alongside accuracy.

items.title: A Symmetry-Matching Approach to Blind-Spot Reduction in Sparse Autoencoders
items.title_zh: 用对称匹配方法减少稀疏自编码器的盲区
items.summary: The author adds a differentiable Gini-based regularisation term to sparse autoencoder training that penalizes uneven perturbation response within a specified family, targeting representation blind spots where semantically distinct inputs are treated as interchangeable. Across GPT-2, Gemma 2 and Qwen 2.5, the term raised lower-tail responses without material degradation in general-text reconstruction.

items.title: ViMoLa: Discrete Motion Tokens for Language-Guided Video Generation
items.title_zh: ViMoLa：用于语言引导视频生成的离散运动 token
items.summary: ViMoLa predicts a motion prior from language and injects it into a frozen image-to-video backbone, compressing dense trajectories into 64 tokens from a 512-entry codebook and predicting them with a 28M-parameter transformer. Trained on 462K videos from Something-Something v2 and Kinetics-400, it raises directional accuracy from 0.287 to 0.442 against a 0.250 chance baseline, while the authors note that control remains imperfect.

items.title: Refusal Is Not Robustness: Measuring Harmful Reachability in Autoregressive Language Models
items.title_zh: 拒绝不等于鲁棒：衡量自回归语言模型中的有害可达性
items.summary: The authors introduce bounded continuation analysis (BCA), which models autoregressive generation as a stochastic process and estimates the probability of reaching harmful continuations rather than relying only on sampled attack success rates. Across four instruction-tuned LLMs and 100 JailbreakBench behaviors, they report that BCA quantifies hidden harmful behavior and can help direct red-team effort.
